name: All Things Open 2026
why: Large open-source developer conference in downtown Raleigh (Raleigh Convention Center), with Google, OpenSSF and MySQL listed as sponsors. A dense room of NC developers for an SDK/API-first wearable.
ask: Attend 10/19-20 and ask organizers about a hallway demo or a 2027 lightning-talk slot on open wearable data
opener: Hi, we're Vybe, building a screenless overnight band that records ECG-based HRV and resting heart rate, with a licensed SDK and API for developers. We'll be at All Things Open in Raleigh. Is there a hallway-track or lightning-talk format where a small hardware SDK could show its open docs, now or for 2027?

name: Hack_NCState 2027
why: NC State's largest annual hackathon: 24-hour event at Talley Student Union, teams of 2-4, industry-sponsored tracks, free for university students. 2026 edition ran Feb 14-15 with a Jan 31 registration deadline.
why_now: 2026 edition ran 2026-02-14/15; 2027 dates not yet published (Feb timing likely, not confirmed)
ask: Ask for the 2027 sponsor packet and propose a wearable-data track prize with loaner DevKits
opener: Hi Hack_NCState team, we're Vybe, building a screenless band that records overnight HRV and resting heart rate, with a developer SDK and API. Students building on wearables keep hitting closed or shrinking APIs. Could we sponsor a small wearable-data prize at Hack_NCState 2027 and lend a few DevKits? Happy to see your sponsor options.

name: HackNC
why: UNC-Chapel Hill's long-running 24-hour student hackathon, which UNC describes as the largest in the Southeast. Recent editions ran Oct 27-29, 2023 and Nov 9-11, 2024. MLH-affiliated in past years.
why_now: Fall timing (late Oct/Nov) in recent years; 2026 dates not found
ask: Ask whether a 2026 or 2027 edition is open to a hardware sponsor offering DevKit loans
opener: Hi HackNC organizers, we're Vybe, a pre-launch wearable that records overnight HRV and resting heart rate, with an SDK and API built for developers. We'd like to support HackNC with a wearable-data challenge and a few loaner DevKits. Is sponsorship open for your next edition, and who should we talk to?

name: Pearl Hacks
why: UNC-Chapel Hill hackathon since 2014, beginner-friendly and built for women and non-binary students 18+; 24-hour team build. A first-time-builder audience suits a simple, documented wearable SDK.
ask: Offer a beginner workshop on reading HRV data from a wearable SDK plus a small prize
opener: Hi Pearl Hacks team, we're Vybe, building a screenless overnight band with an SDK and API for developers. Pearl Hacks' beginner focus fits what we want to test: can a first-time hacker pull wearable data in an afternoon? Could we run a short workshop or sponsor a prize at your next event?

name: HackDuke Code for Good
why: Duke's student-run social-good hackathon. The Feb 8-9, 2025 edition had a Health track (with Finance, Sustainability and Interactive Media); in 2021 Duke Student Affairs sponsored the health track.
why_now: Last confirmed edition 2025-02-09; next dates not found
ask: Sponsor a prize in the Health track and lend DevKits for teams
opener: Hi HackDuke team, we're Vybe, building a screenless band that records overnight HRV and resting heart rate, with a licensed SDK and API. Your Health track is where student teams need real wearable data and rarely get it. Could we sponsor a Health-track prize and lend a few DevKits at your next Code for Good?

name: Duke Center for Computational and Digital Health Innovation (CompHealth)
why: Duke center whose 'Wearables' driving-technology area spans the BIG IDEAs Lab (Dunn) and the Health Innovation Lab (Ryan Shaw). Runs virtual seminars (Oct 7, 2026 talk on wearable/implantable systems) and a Center Demo Day (Sept 25, 2026). Distinct from the existing BIG IDEAs Lab row: this is the center's seminar/demo channel.
why_now: Wearable-systems virtual seminar held 2026-10-07; Demo Day 2026-09-25
ask: Ask to be considered for a future virtual seminar or the next Demo Day as a developer-platform wearable
opener: Hi, we're Vybe, building a screenless overnight band that records ECG-based HRV and resting heart rate, with a licensed SDK and API so researchers own the data pipeline. I saw CompHealth's wearables seminar series and Demo Day. Would a short talk on open wearable data access fit a future seminar, or could we join the next Demo Day?

name: DHIT Digital Health Happy Hours
why: Recurring Triangle networking series for digital-health entrepreneurs, investors and partners, held at American Underground in Durham (e.g. longevity-themed event Oct 22, 2024) and also in Charlotte; listed on NCBiotech and UNC Innovate calendars.
why_now: Most recent dated listing found 2024-10-22; 2026 schedule not found
ask: Attend the next happy hour and offer a 5-minute builder talk on wearable data access
opener: Hi DHIT team, we're Vybe, building a screenless band that records overnight HRV and resting heart rate, with an SDK and API for digital-health builders. With the Fitbit Web API turning off Oct 30, a lot of Triangle teams are re-picking data sources. Could we give a five-minute builder talk at an upcoming Digital Health Happy Hour?

name: Charlotte Hack (UNC Charlotte hackathon club)
why: Official hackathon club at UNC Charlotte; organizes its own events and sends students to other schools' hackathons. Public club email listed on its event page.
ask: Offer 3 loaner DevKits for club members to take to their next hackathon
opener: Hi Charlotte Hack, we're Vybe, building a screenless overnight band with an SDK and API for developers. Your club sends teams to hackathons all over. Would a few members want to take loaner DevKits to their next event and tell us where our docs fall short? We'd cover shipping and credit your team.

name: GDG Charlotte (DevFest Charlotte)
why: Independent Charlotte developer group running an annual DevFest (4th annual on Nov 6, 2025 at UNC Charlotte's Woodward Hall). Google's 2026 DevFest season runs Oct 1-Dec 31, 2026; the Google Health API now replaces the Fitbit Web API.
why_now: DevFest 2026 season runs 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31; Fitbit Web API turned off 2026-10-30
ask: Propose a DevFest or meetup talk: 'Life after the Fitbit Web API: wearable data options for Android devs'
opener: Hi GDG Charlotte, we're Vybe, building a screenless overnight HRV band with an SDK and API. With the legacy Fitbit Web API turning off Oct 30, Android devs are re-planning wearable integrations. Would a neutral talk on wearable data options, with Vybe as one example, fit DevFest Charlotte 2026 or a winter meetup?

name: GDG Chapel Hill (North Carolina DevFest)
why: Runs North Carolina DevFest for the RTP area; the 2025 edition moved online after registrations far exceeded in-person capacity. Google's 2026 DevFest season runs Oct 1-Dec 31.
why_now: DevFest 2026 season open through 2026-12-31; 2026 NC DevFest page not found
ask: Ask about a talk slot at NC DevFest 2026 on Health Connect / Google Health API alternatives

If there's a 2026 edition, would a talk on wearable data access after the Fitbit Web API change be useful? Happy to keep it vendor-neutral.

name: WakeHacks
org: Wake Forest University Department of Computer Science

ask: Sponsor a wearable-data prize at the spring 2027 event

name: UNC/NC State Joint BME Senior Design Program
org: Joint Department of Biomedical Engineering (UNC Chapel Hill & NC State)
why: Two-semester senior design program (mentored by Andrew DiMeo) where BME students find unmet needs and build devices, ending in a design symposium for industry and investors. Teams need hardware platforms with data access.

opener: Hi, we're Vybe, building a screenless band that records overnight HRV and resting heart rate, with a licensed SDK and raw-data API. Your senior design teams build on real platforms. Would one or two teams want to use our DevKit as the hardware base this year? We'd supply kits and engineering time, and ask only for honest feedback.

name: Health Innovation Day 2026 (The Pearl, Charlotte)

Glad to see a NY Show&Tell back. If there's a tool-demo slot, could we show it briefly? If not, we'll just come and listen.

name: Open Wearables (the-momentum/open-wearables)
why: MIT-licensed, self-hosted open-source API that normalizes wearable data (Garmin, Whoop, Polar, Suunto, Apple Health and more); 0.7.0 added Google Health API support, and Momentum publishes Fitbit-shutdown migration guides. Builders hit by API closures use it, so a Vybe provider would reach them.
why_now: Fitbit Web API turned off 2026-10-30; Open Wearables shipped Google Health API support
ask: Contribute a Vybe provider adapter once DevKit v0.1 API docs are public
opener: Hi Open Wearables maintainers, we're Vybe, building a screenless overnight band with ECG-based HRV and resting heart rate and a licensed SDK/API. Your project is where builders land after API closures. When our DevKit docs go public, would you take a PR adding Vybe as a provider, written to your adapter pattern and marked pre-launch?
